pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A brokerage lives on two relationships, the shipper who pays you and the carrier you pay, and the margin in between. This workspace keeps both sides of every load on one row.
From quote to paid
Loads

: one row per shipment. It moves Quoted (rate sent), Tendered (customer said yes), Covered (carrier booked and rate confirmation signed), In transit, Delivered. Margin is the customer rate less carrier pay; Rate per mile helps you compare lanes.
Customers
: shippers, their payment terms and credit limit, with revenue and margin from delivered loads and what they still owe.
Carriers
: every trucking company you work with: MC and USDOT numbers, insurance expiry, cargo cover, safety rating. Only Approved carriers get loads.
Customer invoices
: one per delivered load. The linehaul comes from the load; detention, lumper and other extras are added on the invoice.
A day on the desk
7:00: open Loads, This week view. Anything picking up today and still Tendered is the first job.
Carrier sales works the Loads to cover list: past carriers on the lane first, then the load board.
Before a load is Covered: carrier is Approved, insurance runs past delivery, rate confirmation is signed.
Check calls at pickup, midway and delivery; notes go in the load's page.
Delivered: press Mark delivered when the proof of delivery arrives, then Create invoice the same day.
Friday: billing works Money to collect and pays carriers whose proof of delivery is in.
Reps, carrier sales, billing
A margin you can trust
Quotes and cancelled loads show no margin, so the totals are only freight that moved. Short-paid invoices stay open until the difference is collected or written off by the owner.

text.text: Most broker losses come from the wrong carrier: lapsed insurance, a brand-new authority, or someone pretending to be a real fleet. This page is the setup routine every carrier passes before the first load, and the re-checks that keep the list clean.
Before the first load
Add the carrier with Pending setup. Enter MC and USDOT numbers exactly.
Look up the authority record yourself. Active for at least 90 days, and the phone and email match what the carrier gave you.
Ask for the certificate of insurance from the insurance agent, not from the carrier. Auto liability and cargo, with our company as certificate holder.
Read the safety rating and recent roadside inspections. Conditional means the owner decides.
Collect the W-9, payment details and the signed broker-carrier agreement.
Press Approve carrier. It stamps Approved on.
Red flags

cells.text: Email domain differs from the one on the authority
Possible identity theft; call the listed number
Classic fraud; confirm by phone with a known contact
Insurance certificate sent directly by the carrier
May be altered; get it from the agent
Brand-new authority and a very low rate

text.text: Keeping the list clean
Insurance expiring within 30 days: move to Insurance expiring and request a renewed certificate.
A carrier that drops a load, fakes a check call or re-brokers your freight moves to Do not use, with the reason in its page. Do not delete it; the record protects the next broker.
Once a quarter, sort Carriers by Loads delivered. The top ten get first call on their lanes.
Checklist before tendering
Carrier is Approved
Insurance runs past the delivery date
Equipment matches the load
Rate confirmation signed and returned
Driver name and cell number confirmed by a call to the carrier's listed dispatch phone, not a number from an email
A load is a promise to two people at once. This page is the routine from the shipper's yes to the signed proof of delivery, so the customer never has to ask where their freight is.
When the customer tenders
Move the load from Quoted to Tendered and press Assign to me.
Fill the load sheet: appointment times, commodity, weight, special handling, reference numbers.
Price the carrier side before you call. Target margin on dry van is 15 to 20 percent; reefer and flatbed often less.
Covering it
Call carriers who hauled this lane before. Their Loads delivered count and notes are on the carrier row.
Agree the rate, send the rate confirmation, and tick Rate confirmation signed only when it comes back.
Move the load to Covered and set the carrier.
Check calls

cells.text: Trailer and seal numbers, loaded time
Arrival time, so detention can be billed
Proof of delivery photo and any shortage or damage

text.text: Press Mark picked up at the first call and Mark delivered when the proof of delivery arrives.
When things go wrong
Truck breaks down: tell the customer before they ask, with a new arrival time.
Detention: write in and out times in the load page; it goes on the invoice as Detention and extras.
Load cancelled by the shipper after cover: agree a truck-order-not-used fee with both sides in writing.
Worked example

Salinas to Phoenix strawberries: tendered at 3,150, covered with a reefer carrier at 2,700 for a 450 margin, about 14 percent. Pickup at 4 am; the reefer temperature is confirmed on the bill of lading at the first check call. The receiver signs clean the next afternoon, the broker presses Mark delivered, and billing sends the invoice before close.
The live board for the floor: what still needs a truck, what picks up today, and what is rolling. Check calls are written on the load's page.
Carriers to watch

Three things eat a broker's margin after the truck is booked: a cargo claim, detention at the dock, and a truck ordered not used. Each one has a rule written into the rate confirmation; this page is how we work them.
Detention
The rate confirmation says the free time (usually two hours) and the hourly rate after it.
The driver texts in and out times; the carrier sends the signed in-and-out sheet. No sheet, no detention.
Bill the shipper the same rate you pay the carrier, as an accessorial on the Customer invoice. Never eat detention to keep a customer quiet; tell them the dock is slow.
Truck ordered, not used (TONU)
When the shipper cancels after the truck is dispatched, the carrier is owed a TONU fee, usually $150 to $300.
Mark the load Cancelled, add the fee as an accessorial on the invoice, and pay the carrier the same week.
Cargo claims
Get the delivery receipt with the exception written on it, and photos, the same day.
Tell the carrier in writing within 24 hours and ask for their insurer's claim number.
The shipper files the claim with its invoice for the goods; we pass it to the carrier and chase it.
Do not short-pay the carrier on your own; agree any offset in writing first.
Write every step on the load's page with the date.

cells.text: Bill and pay detention, both sides

Talk to the carrier; two strikes and they leave the list
